reviews.title: Unacceptable customer service, and cancellation practice
reviews.text:
AT&T – Unacceptable Customer Service, Billing Issues, and Cancellation Practices

I’ve been an AT&T customer paying over $800 per month because I have multiple lines on my account. Today, I’ve spent the entire day trying to unlock a phone that is already paid off in full and cancel two lines that I no longer need.

I’ve spent over FOUR HOURS on hold, been transferred repeatedly, and received FOUR promises of callbacks without any resolution.

Opening a new line with AT&T is incredibly easy, but trying to cancel one is an absolute nightmare! You can’t cancel in person, they direct you to customer service or the app, and neither option has worked for me.

I am paying a substantial amount of money every month, yet I cannot get basic customer service or make changes to my own account. I feel trapped, financially affected, and completely disrespected as a customer.

I am now seriously considering legal action and urgently seeking legal representation to protect my consumer rights.

AT&T needs to be held accountable for how it treats paying customers. This is unacceptable, exhausting, and one of the worst customer service experiences I’ve ever had.

Managing services, checking outages, finding service details, downloading bills, updating AutoPay, or changing notification settings should be effortless. Instead, everything feels buried behind a frustrating, poorly organized interface.

Leaving AT&T for Verizon was the best decision I’ve made, and dealing with this company has been nothing short of a nightmare. Their business model seems built entirely on bait-and-switch tactics, hidden charges, and intentionally impossible customer service loops.
During my time with them, my monthly bill fluctuated wildly—going from $107 to $350, $250, $200, $210, and $160 unpredictably. After countless frustrating calls, I was repeatedly promised that $167 would finally be my fixed rate, only for them to sneak it back up to $185 and eventually standardize it at $210.
To top it all off, after I switched carriers and couldn't even access AT&T service anymore, they hit me with a staggering $207 charge for a brief 31-minute international call. I never requested international calling features, and getting penalized like this feels predatory and completely in bad faith.
Add in the fact that their network speed was great the very first month only to crawl like dial-up for the rest of my contract, and that reaching customer service takes hours of waiting, it is clear they take advantage of consumers who don't have the time or energy to fight back. They hook you in with a low quote, lock you in, and end up charging triple what was agreed. Stay far away from this company.
